title: py-sdk: streaming chat event coordinator + backpressure-friendly ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Users find our raw streaming event surface (token deltas, raw SSE frames) hard to compose for robust chat experiences that need function-call events, tool signals, metadata updates, and graceful reconnects. Current examples focus on raw iterators and ad-hoc middleware; we need a coordinated ergonomic API that makes backpressure, deduplication, and resume behavior easy and predictable.

Goal: Design and implement an EventCoordinator abstraction in the Python SDK that sits on top of the streaming transport (SSE/gRPC), exposes a small set of composable primitives (AsyncSignalHandler, StreamSession, SignalMiddleware), provides built-in backpressure helpers, deterministic resume semantics (resume tokens + sequence watermarking), and a cookbook of examples for common patterns (function-calling flows, tool handoffs, partial-response UX). Deliver library code, unit/integration tests, examples, and docs for migration from the current streaming iterator patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Public API: StreamSession/StreamEvent/AsyncSignalHandler documented with code examples for: token streaming, function-call events, structured tool payloads
Backpressure: SDK provides a built-in bounded consumer queue and a context-manager ergonomic wrapper so synchronous code can consume streams without uncontrolled memory growth
Resume semantics: SDK can resume a disconnected stream using resume tokens and sequence numbers; end-to-end tests validate at-least-once delivery with dedupe helper
Retries: Transparent reconnect + replay logic with configurable retry policy and clear hooks for user code to re-run side effects
Docs: Cookbook with 4 examples (simple token loop, function-call extraction, tool-handoff flow, resumable consumer) published in docs site

Tests: Unit tests for coordinator logic, integration tests exercising real server streams (simulated via test harness), and performance benchmark showing <5% overhead vs raw iterator under a 100 concurrent streams workload
Migration notes: short guide for existing users showing how to swap iterator code for StreamSession and known caveats
technical_notes: API sketch: StreamSession = async context manager that yields a StreamEvent async iterator plus an EventCoordinator object with helpers (checkpoint(), watermark, close()).
StreamEvent: typed wrapper with fields: kind={token,function_call,metadata,error,done}, text_fragment, seq_num, resume_token(optional), structured_payload(optional)

Backpressure: default consumer queue size 64; SDK exposes BlockingStream wrapper for sync consumers that uses a background asyncio loop + queue.put with timeout for configurable policy (drop/raise/block).

Resume: server provides opaque resume_token + monotonically increasing seq_num per session; client will request resume with last seen resume_token and last_seq_num to allow server to skip already-ACKed messages. Deduping uses (session_id, seq_num).

Retries: retry policy is exponential backoff with jitter, max_attempts configurable. On reconnect, EventCoordinator can optionally invoke a user-provided on_replay hook so application can re-emit idempotent events or reconcile state.
Testing: add a stream harness in tests/fixtures that can inject delays, reorder frames, duplicate frames to validate dedupe/resume logic.
Compatibility: keep lowest-level streaming iterator intact; EventCoordinator composed on top, so users can adopt incrementally.
Telemetry: emit coordinator.telemetry events for reconnects, replays, dropped-messages, and queue-overflow so Console can show per-token cost & reliability signals.
Performance: aim for <1 alloc per token in fast-path; measure with existing benchmark suite (runtime-1.18 benchmark harness).
implementation_plan: Design RFC and API doc: draft and review with SDK, runtime, and docs (3 days)
Core implementation: EventCoordinator + StreamSession + adapters for existing streaming transports (5 days)
Sync wrapper + blocking queue: implement blocking consumer helper and context-manager for sync code (2 days)
Integrations: add hooks for Console telemetry and for retry policy from runtime (2 days)
Tests: unit + integration harness with fault injection (3 days)
Docs & cookbook: 4 example notebooks + migration guide (2 days)
Review & polish: API review with DX/Design, perf tuning, cut release (2 days)
Total: ~19 dev days distributed across 2 engineers with parallel workstreams
